videos.title: Celltype — agentic drug company launch
videos.metrics: Original post: @ycombinator on X, created 2026-02-18T16:00:02Z. Verified via cdn.syndication.twimg.com tweet-result API (x.com HTML blocked, HTTP 402): favorite_count=231, conversation_count(replies)=20; view count not exposed by that API — candidate note claims ~44.7k views, unverified. No higher-engagement original found: CellType's own YC launch page (ycombinator.com/companies/celltype) shows no upvote/engagement counters, and no @celltypeinc post of this video with better numbers surfaced. Seen 2026-08-05. Context: ~0.5% like/view rate on a ~1M-follower account; YC launch tweets that break out land in the thousands of likes / hundreds of thousands of views. The often-cited "7M+ views" belongs to Sundar Pichai's earlier Cell2Sentence post, not this launch video.
videos.reason: Reject on engagement only. 231 likes / 20 replies (~44.7k claimed views) on the @ycombinator launch post is middling for X — not a clear standout, and engagement is the filter. Craft-wise it would have been a good clone target: 71 s, 1920x1080, zero live-action people across 10 sampled frames — the whole film is kinetic typography (all-caps grotesque, word-per-beat cuts, stat counters like "75%", stacked light/bold pairs) over stock nature plates, macro lab shots and 3D cell/tumor renders, closing on a Sundar Pichai pull-quote card. Downloaded fine (21.4 MB) but note video.twimg.com only resolves over IPv4 here: curl -4 is required, plain curl hangs and exits 28.

videos.title: Okara — world's first AI CMO launch
videos.metrics: 14,045,415 views / 27,333 likes / 2,358 RTs / 1,601 replies (fxtwitter API re-confirmed 2026-08-05; posted 2026-03-16; account 72,502 followers). 53.5s, 1784x1080@60fps, 7.98MB.
videos.producedLayer: Device comp (app rendered in rounded card with drop shadow on warm cream backdrop, never raw full-screen), edited time-compressed cut rhythm (8 hard cuts across 53s compressing a minutes-long agent workflow into an escalating montage), opening title/hero beat (logo + tagline + single URL input), and a persistent terminal typewriter-text strip that functions as kinetic narrative text. No motion graphics, brand cards, or camera moves — the produced layer is real but thin; a clone must lean on the card comp, terminal-type beat, and cut rhythm.
videos.reusability: Highly credible: the grammar (hero input beat → terminal typewriter narration → cursor-led dashboard reveals in a floating card, time-compressed cuts) is product-agnostic — any agentic SaaS drops in cleanly, with all dashboard/doc screens as product slots; only the pixel-skull mascot is brand-specific and it is replaceable content.
videos.reason: Engagement is genuinely film-driven (27.3k likes = ~38% of a 72.5k follower base, 14M views = ~190x; small startup, no brand halo). Zero humans — an earlier founders frame turned out to be another parallel agent's candidate overwriting x_10.jpg in the shared vet2 dir; unique-prefix re-extraction confirmed all 53s is screen-UI. A real produced layer exists (card device comp on cream backdrop, opening title beat, terminal typewriter narration, 8-cut time-compressed rhythm) so it is not a raw feature demo, though the layer is thin — the clone's value hinges on nailing the terminal-type beat and cut rhythm with dashboards as product slots. Downloaded and verified at the target path.

videos.title: Endex — AI agent inside Excel ($14M OpenAI Startup Fund raise film)
videos.metrics: 10,835,274 views / 8,035 likes / 2,087 replies / 440 RTs (fxtwitter API, confirmed 2026-08-05; posted 2025-08-06). Like:view ratio 0.07% implies partly promoted views and the invite CTA inflates replies, but 8k likes from a 7k-follower account is genuine film-driven traction with zero brand halo.
videos.producedLayer: Retro iMac CRT prop cold-open with glitching serif type; black serif title cards ("Microsoft Excel", "Endex") closing the film; Excel window composited over a desk scene with shadow and push-in camera moves; styled kinetic captions throughout; edited cut rhythm alternating founder bookends with the UI demo spine.
videos.reusability: The grammar — serif type cards, screen-UI desk comps with push-ins, captioned agent-demo beats — is product-agnostic and another screen-UI product drops in credibly; only the founder bookends and the live-action iMac prop shot need substitution with type/product beats.
videos.reason: Engagement is film-borne (7k-follower account, 8k likes/2k replies, no brand halo even after discounting promoted views); humans are ~30% bookend interview footage while the spine is Excel screen-UI comps and serif type beats; a clear multi-axis produced layer exists; grammar suits OpenDemo's screen-UI and type engines; 4K master downloaded and frame-verified.

videos.title: Sorce — Tinder for Jobs (YC launch)
videos.metrics: 2,775,088 views / 3,567 likes / 374 RTs / 293 replies (fxtwitter API, confirmed 2026-08-05; posted 2025-10-06 on @ycombinator)
videos.producedLayer: Real produced film: cinematic camera work and an edited cut rhythm (doorway dolly, face close-ups, prop inserts like a handwritten Rejections tally, macro shots of a rejection email and the app on a physical phone). But zero rebuildable graphics grammar: no title/type beats, no device comps (UI is only ever a camera-filmed physical phone screen), no brand cards, no motion graphics.
videos.reusability: Poor — the grammar is location-shot live-action narrative (actor, props, natural light); dropping another product in would require a reshoot with people, not a config swap, and nothing here is expressible with textcards/cinematic3d.
videos.reason: Engagement is genuinely the film's (8-10x likes and ~40x views over the same account's typical launch posts, so not brand halo), and it downloads fine — but frame review shows a live-action human-narrative short: the protagonist dominates 7 of 10 sampled frames and the story arc IS the film; app UI appears only as a camera-filmed physical phone screen. Dominant live-action humans is an automatic reject per runbook rule 3, and reusability is poor since none of it maps to our type/device-comp/motion-graphics engines.

videos.title: Chad IDE — "the brainrot code editor" (YC launch)
videos.metrics: 3,397,926 views / 3,212 likes / 629 replies / 154 RTs / 1,028 quotes (fxtwitter API, 2026-08-05). 74.3s 1920x1080 30fps confirmed via ffprobe.
videos.producedLayer: Real but thin: edited comedy cut rhythm, live-action prop close-ups (Newport pack macro at t2), one kinetic title beat ("Chad / the brainrot IDE" yellow type over dimmed UI, ~t58-66), GigaChad meme end card (t72). The middle ~60% is raw IDE screen capture (Stake Plinko, Clash Royale, Claude Code panel) with the founders' live webcam permanently embedded in the UI.
videos.reusability: Poor — the grammar is a bespoke founder-skit satire whose spine is the two founders performing on camera plus borrowed meme/third-party IP (GigaChad, Stake casino, Clash Royale, Newport); strip the humans and memes and only a generic screen capture with one title card remains, so another product cannot credibly be dropped in.
videos.reason: Engagement is genuinely the film's (~10x typical @ycombinator post, 1,028 quote-tweets = organic meme spread, scored 7 after brand-halo discount and noting the weak 0.09% like/view ratio), and it is downloadable — but frame sampling confirms the flagged risk: humans are dominant (live-action skit open at t9/t16, founders' webcam performance embedded in the UI across t23-t58, GigaChad meme close), and the produced layer is a thin comedy edit over raw screen capture whose humor depends on people and licensed meme imagery our textcards/cinematic3d engines cannot rebuild. Fails the humans-not-dominant and reusability gates; reject per runbook section 3.
